fields.title: 2. Event ② — Boost Mobile acquisition/lease talks: reports vs. filings
fields.md:
| Date (US) | Fact | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| 2025-09-08 | EchoStar–SpaceX **spectrum sale and commercial agreement**: AWS-4 and H-block licenses for about **$17.0 billion** (up to $8.5 billion in cash + up to $8.5 billion in SpaceX stock), plus SpaceX covering about $2.0 billion of EchoStar's debt interest (through 2027-11). Commercial agreement: **next-generation Starlink Direct to Cell access for Boost Mobile subscribers** | ② (counterparty IR) [EchoStar press release](https://ir.echostar.com/news-releases/news-release-details/echostar-announces-spectrum-sale-and-commercial-agreement-spacex), 2025-09-08 (403 in this issue — confirmed via reprints and search summaries) |
| 2025-11-05 | Addition: unpaired AWS-3 license for about $2.6 billion (SpaceX stock) | ① [EchoStar 8-K Ex.99 2025-11-06](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000141540425000049/tmb-20251106xex99.htm) |
| As of 2026-09-30 | SpaceX 10-Q: license purchase agreements for **50MHz** (2025-09-07) + **15MHz** (2025-11-05), counterparty 'Spectrum Business Trust 2025-1', the trust pays EchoStar's debt interest **through at least 2027-11-30**, prepaid asset **$856M**. Before final closing (October issue 1-2) | ① [10-Q main text Note 6](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/spcx-20260930.htm) · [10-Q R58](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R58.htm) |

| 2026-10-20 | CFO (earnings call): the goal is "to become a major mobile carrier in the US" — **a statement, section 7** | ② (call statement — quoted in press) [Yahoo Finance 11/02](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-weighs-boost-mobile-deal-in-push-for-starlink-phone-service-report-160901851.html) |
| **2026-11-02** | **Report**: SpaceX is in preliminary talks with EchoStar on **acquiring Boost Mobile or gaining network access**. Musk asked Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile to purchase network capacity, but **all three declined**. Boost is an MVNO with no base stations of its own, leasing the AT&T and T-Mobile networks — lease contracts are generally non-transferable, so consent from the two carriers may be needed. EchoStar has about 7.5 million subscribers (Boost + Gen Mobile). Price and structure not reported. **No statement from either company** | ⑥ [TechCrunch 11/02](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/02/spacex-reportedly-wants-to-buy-boost-mobile-to-compete-with-att-t-mobile-and-verizon/) · [Yahoo Finance 11/02](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-weighs-boost-mobile-deal-in-push-for-starlink-phone-service-report-160901851.html) · [FOX 9 11/02 (citing Reuters and WP)](https://www.fox9.com/news/spacex-boost-mobile-network-report) — Reuters original not viewed in this issue |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K** (latest 10/26) · **No EchoStar 8-K** (latest 2026-10-02 Items 1.01 and 2.01 — end of DISH DBS restructuring and reconnection, unrelated to SpaceX) · EchoStar 3Q26 10-Q not filed (latest 2026-08-03) | ① [SpaceX EDGAR](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json) · [EchoStar EDGAR](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001415404.json) · [EchoStar 8-K 10/02](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000141540426000048/sats-20261001x8k.htm), checked 2026-11-03 |

**What is confirmed as fact (filings)**: SpaceX and EchoStar are already tied together by the purchase of 65MHz of spectrum, the interest reimbursement, and D2C access for Boost subscribers (10-Q · EchoStar 8-K). **What is not confirmed**: the Boost acquisition/network-access talks themselves (two reports — Fox 9 cites both WP and Reuters, but the Reuters original was not viewed), the refusal by the three carriers (reported), and the deal price and structure (not reported). Until a filing appears, **it is not used in the verdict** (source: table above).

### 2-1. What this event touches

| Item | Content | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Axis A · A-2028-1 (30 million subscribers AND separately disclosed D2C revenue of $3.0 billion) | If D2C (Starlink Mobile) gets a **terrestrial-network fallback**, the limits on indoor and urban coverage are removed (reported). However, there is still no separate revenue disclosure — not a milestone input | Progress maintained · background recorded |
| Competition timeline 'US mobile carriers (big three)' (October issue 1-7) | October issue verdict: "SpaceX is the side posing the threat." This report says the three carriers **declined MVNO capacity sales** — meaning SpaceX's terrestrial path is narrowing from 'MVNO lease' to 'MVNO acquisition (Boost) or self-build' (reported). TD Cowen: self-build would be "$80 billion or more, several years" (opinion) | No change in verdict · evidence added |
| Regulation | The FCC 10/29 NPRM (T8 ⑥) is a proposal that would let satellite operators **directly acquire** the underlying terrestrial spectrum licenses — the same direction as Boost's assets (EchoStar's remaining licenses and MVNO contract). A Boost acquisition could be subject to FCC license-transfer review (scope of Boost's own licenses unconfirmed) and HSR | Separate from T8 — **T9 newly created** |
| Probability rules R1–R6 | Not in the conditions | Not triggered |
| Financials | Price not reported — no numbers. Reference only: EchoStar's regulatory-authorization assets held for sale of $16.8 billion (2Q26) relate to the spectrum transaction | Not adopted |

(Source: `state.milestones[A-2028-1]` · `reports/2026-10.md` 1-7 · `reports/2026-11.md` 1-2 · [Yahoo Finance 11/02](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-weighs-boost-mobile-deal-in-push-for-starlink-phone-service-report-160901851.html) · [SeekingAlpha (EchoStar 2Q26)](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20603691))

**Note on the news monitor's classification**: Both reports came in with `trigger_id: null` — meaning there was no slot in the existing triggers, and that judgment was correct (T8 is D2D regulation and deals; Boost is terrestrial MVNO). Going forward, **T9 (Boost/EchoStar deal)** and **T10 (Colossus turbine lawsuit)** are set up as the slots for items of the same kind (source: `data/spacex_watch.json` due · section 5).
